topic: Can the filter's suppression of 19th harmonics improve transponder power efficiency in dense payload configurations?
consensus_response: Non-linear amplifiers, key driver of intermodulation products (IMDs) and ISI, necessitate advanced equalization techniques to mitigate both ISI and ACI.  Filter bandwidth directly impacts spectral efficiency and power consumption. Narrower filters offer higher spectral efficiency but increase complexity. Careful design balancing performance and efficiency is crucial in dense payloads. DLB emphasizes the physical layer aspects while acknowledging system impact.
reference_context: Satellite amplifiers are inherently nonlinear, leading to intermodulation products (IMPs) causing signal distortion.  Linear distortions from channel filtering are of secondary importance compared to the non-linear effects. IMPs contribute significantly to spectral efficiency degradation and capacity limitations.  Minimizing IMPs through efficient filter design and equalization is crucial for achieving high spectral efficiency and power efficiency in dense payloads.
